record.title: Diagnosis and therapeutic management of Babesia gibsoni-induced paraplegia in dogs
record.journal: International Journal of Veterinary Sciences and Animal Husbandry
record.abstract: Two dogs presented to VCC, PGIVAS, Akola, with an inability to walk as the primary complaint, accompanied by fever, inappetence for one week, and vomiting. Clinical examination revealed mild to high rectal temperatures (102.5-104 ?), swollen lymph nodes, congested mucous membranes, prolonged capillary refill time, tachycardia, polypnea, paraplegia, and mild tick infestation. Hematobiochemical analysis showed thrombocytopenia, neutrophilic leukocytosis, elevated BUN and creatinine, borderline hypoproteinemia, and increased SGOT, while other parameters were within normal limits. Diagnosis was established based on blood smear, immunochromatographic test (ICT), and confirmed by PCR. Both dogs were treated with artesunate and azithromycin, along with supportive therapy including neurotropic vitamins, methylprednisolone, proton pump inhibitors, and polyherbal liver and platelet stimulants. Both dogs demonstrated uneventful recovery by day 10th and 30th post-treatment, with normalization of clinical and hematobiochemical parameters, and parasitological testing confirmed complete clearance of the infection by day 30th post-treatment.

screening.rationale: Two dogs with B. gibsoni-associated paraplegia, a distinct neurological complication; largely diagnostic/treatment description but syndromic.
